cases.title: Why glass is endlessly recyclable and mostly is not recycled

skeleton.brief: Glass can be endlessly recycled without degrading
Explain the glass recycling loop from bottle to new bottle
Every step works except sorting, which breaks the loop
Mixed-colour cullet downgrades the batch, causing issues
US recycles one-third of glass; Sweden recycles over ninety percent
Difference is separate colour collection, not technology
More cullet reduces furnace energy use and carbon footprint
what it all adds up to
The problem is the bin, not the glass material itself

narration.text: Glass can be endlessly recycled without degrading.

slot_quote.heading: "Glass is the one packaging material that can go round forever."
bullets: — Explainer Video

narration.text: The glass recycling loop is short: a bottle is collected, sorted by colour, crushed into cullet, melted with sand and soda ash at about fifteen hundred degrees, formed into a new bottle, filled, and sold again.
Every step in the recycling loop works except sorting, which breaks the loop.

slot_myth_fact.myth: All steps in glass recycling work perfectly.
slot_myth_fact.fact: Sorting is the step that breaks the recycling loop.
slot_myth_fact.heading: Sorting breaks the loop

narration.text: Mixed-colour cullet downgrades the batch because it can only become green glass or aggregate. A single broken brown bottle in a clear stream ruins the batch.
In the United States, about one-third of glass containers get recycled, while in Sweden it is over ninety percent.
The difference is not technology, but separate colour collection instead of a commingled bin.

slot_stat.heading: Separate colour collection matters
bullets: Not advanced technology, but sorting method

narration.text: Every ten percent of cullet in the mix cuts furnace energy by around three percent, reducing the carbon footprint.

slot_stat.heading: More cullet reduces energy use
bullets: 10% more cullet cuts furnace energy by 3%
Furnace accounts for most carbon in a bottle

narration.text: Fixing sorting and increasing cullet use could significantly reduce energy use and emissions in glass production.

slot_proportion.heading: Energy use in glass production
slot_proportion.caption: Furnace energy dominates the carbon footprint

narration.text: The problem is the bin, not the glass material itself.

cases.title: What inflation actually measures

skeleton.brief: Inflation is not just prices going up
Inflation measures money value against a fixed shopping basket
Statistics agency selects and weights goods in the basket
Housing, transport, and food have largest weights in basket
Weighted changes affect inflation index differently than averages
Personal inflation differs from headline due to individual spending
Core inflation excludes volatile food and energy prices
Core inflation shows a narrower, more stable inflation signal
Inflation numbers are real but answer a narrower question

narration.text: Inflation is not the price of things going up. It is the value of money going down.

slot_quote.heading: Inflation is not the price of things going up.
bullets: — It is the value of money going down

narration.text: Inflation is measured against a fixed shopping basket. This basket contains a selection of goods and services whose prices are tracked over time to see how money's value changes.

slot_term.definition: A fixed list of goods and services used to measure inflation by tracking price changes over time.
slot_term.caption: Used by statistics agencies to measure inflation
slot_term.heading: Shopping Basket

narration.text: A statistics agency selects a few hundred goods and services, weights them by actual spending, and prices the same list every month to calculate inflation.

slot_cycle.heading: How inflation is calculated
slot_cycle.caption: A repeating process by the statistics agency

narration.text: In a typical basket, housing is about a third of the weight, transport around fifteen percent, food thirteen, and everything else shares the remainder.

slot_proportion.heading: Weight distribution in the basket
slot_proportion.caption: Housing, transport, and food have the largest weights

narration.text: Weighted changes affect the inflation index differently than simple averages. For example, a big rise in rent impacts inflation more than a fall in TV prices.

slot_myth_fact.myth: Inflation is just the average price change of all goods.
slot_myth_fact.fact: Weighted changes mean big categories like housing affect inflation more than smaller ones like TVs.
slot_myth_fact.heading: Inflation weighting matters

narration.text: Your personal inflation may differ from the headline figure because you don't buy the average basket. If you rent and commute, your inflation might be higher.

slot_myth_fact.fact: Personal spending patterns cause individual inflation to vary from the headline.
slot_myth_fact.heading: Personal inflation differs

narration.text: Core inflation excludes food and energy prices because they are volatile and can mask underlying trends.

slot_stat.heading: Core inflation excludes food and energy
bullets: These prices swing due to weather and war, hiding other signals

narration.text: Core inflation provides a narrower, more stable signal by removing volatile food and energy prices, helping economists see underlying inflation trends more clearly.
Inflation numbers are real but answer a narrower question than most people think.

bullets: It measures average price changes weighted by spending

cases.title: How a delivery text scam works

skeleton.brief: Introduce the scam message about undelivered parcel and fee
Explain timing targets people expecting parcels on Tuesday afternoons
Sender uses mobile number, not official courier short code
Link mimics courier domain but is controlled by scammer
Page requests small fee; real goal is card details and voluntary input
Follow-up call from bank fraud team to get authentication code
Scam’s structure: plausible ask then urgent second contact
Understanding scam’s shape helps recognize and avoid it

narration.text: You get a message saying your parcel couldn't be delivered and asks for a small fee.

asset_request.guidance: A clear close-up of a phone screen with a scam text about a parcel and fee, no personal info visible.

narration.text: The message arrives on a Tuesday afternoon, a time when many people expect parcels. The scam only needs to fool those who actually have a delivery due, not everyone.
